newsitem.title: CHINA: China foreign minister to visit United States.
newsitem.headline: China foreign minister to visit United States.

text.p: Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen is to visit the United States later this month and will meet President Bill Clinton, a spokesman said on Tuesday.
Qian will visit the United States at the invitation of his U.S. counterpart Madeleine Albright, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a regular news briefing.
Qian's discussions with Albright would be wide-ranging and would focus on Sino-U.S. problems and issues of mutual concern to China and the United States, Cui said.
"(Qian) will talk with Albright on Sino-U.S. relations and international issues of mutual concern to China and the United States," he said.
"I believe the talks will be wide-ranging and profound," he said.
Qian would also meet Clinton and U.S. Vice President Al Gore, he said.

Gore visited China last month, becoming the most senior U.S. official to go to China since the 1989 military crackdown on student-led pro-democracy demonstrations centred in Beijing's Tiananmen Square.
Gore's trip was viewed as paving the way for an exchange of presidential visits later this year and in 1998.
Sino-U.S. ties have improved in recent months, after plunging in 1995 and early 1996 amid disputes over human rights, Taiwan and trade.
